title: Why are we trying to go to Mars
paragraphs: It sounds like something from the realms of science fiction – a space expedition into the vast expanse of space, heading towards the Red Planet. While we’re not quite ready to put a person on terra firma, the question we ask today is: why are so many countries interested in going to Mars?

The space race saw the USA and USSR compete to achieve firsts in spaceflight. The Soviet Union released Sputnik 1, an artificial satellite, before anyone else, and the US landed on the Moon first. Now it appears that Mars is the celestial body of desire. While the kudos and bragging rights to be the first nation to touchdown is an obvious draw, there are other reasons we want to get there. One of these could be the survival of our species. You only have to look at the fossilised remains of the dinosaurs to see the benefit of finding another habitable planet. While Mars doesn’t have the right conditions to call it home just yet, there’s always the concept of terraforming – changing the environment of a planet to suit our needs.

However, not everyone agrees. Leading astrophysicist Neil deGrasse Tyson has said the concept of altering habitability of another planet because of the damage we have done to Earth makes no sense when we can simply terraform Earth.

It seems the main reason at the moment is the search for extraterrestrial life. It has long been believed that, at one time, Mars was abundant with life. Now seemingly dead, the potential fossils could answer questions about our own evolution and that of our planet. One theory is that bacterial life on our planet didn’t start here, but was transferred via asteroid from Mars.

One benefit championed by scientists like Neil deGrasse Tyson is that landing on Mars may inspire more people to become interested in science and astronomy. Surely inspiring a new generation to visit the stars is reason enough.

vocabulary.entry: space expedition /speɪs ˌekspəˈdɪʃn/ n. 星际探险
vocabulary.example: The space expedition is scheduled to launch next year.
vocabulary.translation: 这项星际探险计划定于明年启动。

vocabulary.entry: vast expanse /vɑːst ɪkˈspæns/ n. 浩瀚的区域
vocabulary.example: The ship sailed across a vast expanse of ocean.
vocabulary.translation: 这艘船驶过了一片浩瀚的海洋。

vocabulary.entry: Red Planet /red ˈplænɪt/ n. 红色星球（指火星）
vocabulary.example: Scientists are studying the Red Planet for signs of water.
vocabulary.translation: 科学家们正在研究这颗红色星球，寻找水存在的迹象。

vocabulary.entry: terra firma /ˌterə ˈfɜːmə/ n. 陆地；坚实的地面
vocabulary.example: After weeks at sea, they were glad to be back on terra firma.
vocabulary.translation: 在海上漂泊数周后，他们很高兴能重返陆地。

vocabulary.entry: space race /speɪs reɪs/ n. 太空竞赛
vocabulary.example: The space race between the two superpowers lasted for decades.
vocabulary.translation: 两个超级大国之间的太空竞赛持续了数十年。

vocabulary.entry: spaceflight /ˈspeɪsflaɪt/ n. 航天飞行
vocabulary.example: The company is developing new technology for commercial spaceflight.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司正在研发商业航天飞行的新技术。

vocabulary.entry: artificial satellite /ˌɑːtɪfɪʃl ˈsætəlaɪt/ n. 人造卫星
vocabulary.example: The artificial satellite can transmit data back to Earth.
vocabulary.translation: 这颗人造卫星能将数据传输回地球。

vocabulary.entry: celestial body /səˈlestɪəl ˈbɒdi/ n. 天体
vocabulary.example: The moon is a celestial body that orbits the Earth.
vocabulary.translation: 月球是一颗围绕地球运行的天体。

vocabulary.entry: kudos /ˈkjuːdɒs/ n. 荣誉；赞誉
vocabulary.example: The team earned great kudos for their successful project.
vocabulary.translation: 该团队凭借这个成功的项目赢得了高度赞誉。

vocabulary.entry: bragging right /ˈbræɡɪŋ raɪt/ n. 吹嘘的资本
vocabulary.example: Winning the championship gave them the bragging right for years.
vocabulary.translation: 赢得冠军让他们有了可以吹嘘多年的资本。

vocabulary.entry: touchdown /ˈtʌtʃdaʊn/ n. （航天器的）着陆
vocabulary.example: The touchdown of the rover on Mars was broadcast live worldwide.
vocabulary.translation: 火星探测器的着陆过程向全球进行了直播。

vocabulary.entry: survival /səˈvaɪvl/ n. 生存；存活
vocabulary.example: The survival of the species depends on finding a new habitat.
vocabulary.translation: 该物种的生存取决于能否找到新的栖息地。

vocabulary.entry: fossilised remain /ˈfɒsəlaɪzd rɪˈmeɪn/ n. 化石残骸
vocabulary.example: The fossilised remain of the ancient animal was discovered in the desert.
vocabulary.translation: 这具远古动物的化石残骸是在沙漠中发现的。

vocabulary.entry: habitable planet /ˈhæbɪtəbl ˈplænɪt/ n. 宜居星球
vocabulary.example: Astronomers are searching for habitable planets outside the solar system.
vocabulary.translation: 天文学家正在太阳系外寻找宜居星球。

vocabulary.entry: terraforming /ˈterəfɔːmɪŋ/ n. 行星地球化改造
vocabulary.example: Terraforming Mars is a long-term goal for many space agencies.
vocabulary.translation: 火星地球化改造是许多航天机构的长期目标。

vocabulary.entry: astrophysicist /ˌæstrəʊˈfɪzɪsɪst/ n. 天体物理学家
vocabulary.example: The renowned astrophysicist gave a lecture on black holes.
vocabulary.translation: 这位著名的天体物理学家做了一场关于黑洞的讲座。

vocabulary.entry: extraterrestrial life /ˌekstrətəˈrestriəl laɪf/ n. 外星生命
vocabulary.example: Many people believe that extraterrestrial life exists in the universe.
vocabulary.translation: 很多人相信宇宙中存在外星生命。

vocabulary.entry: abundant with /əˈbʌndənt wɪð/ 富于；充满
vocabulary.example: The forest is abundant with various species of plants and animals.
vocabulary.translation: 这片森林里充满了各种各样的动植物。

vocabulary.entry: fossil /ˈfɒsl/ n. 化石
vocabulary.example: The museum has a collection of dinosaur fossils.
vocabulary.translation: 这家博物馆收藏了一批恐龙化石。

vocabulary.entry: bacterial life /bækˈtɪəriəl laɪf/ n. 细菌生命
vocabulary.example: Scientists are researching the origin of bacterial life on Earth.
vocabulary.translation: 科学家们正在研究地球上细菌生命的起源。

vocabulary.entry: asteroid /ˈæstərɔɪd/ n. 小行星
vocabulary.example: An asteroid passed close to Earth last month.
vocabulary.translation: 上个月有一颗小行星近距离掠过地球。

vocabulary.entry: astronomy /əˈstrɒnəmi/ n. 天文学
vocabulary.example: She developed an interest in astronomy when she was a child.
vocabulary.translation: 她小时候就对天文学产生了兴趣。

sentences.english: It sounds like something from the realms of science fiction – a space expedition into the vast expanse of space, heading towards the Red Planet.
sentences.chinese: 这听起来像是科幻小说里的情节——一场深入浩瀚太空的星际探险，目标直指那颗红色星球。

sentences.english: While we’re not quite ready to put a person on terra firma, the question we ask today is: why are so many countries interested in going to Mars?
sentences.chinese: 尽管我们还没准备好将人类送上火星表面，但今天我们要探讨的问题是：为什么这么多国家都对火星探索抱有浓厚兴趣？

sentences.english: The space race saw the USA and USSR compete to achieve firsts in spaceflight.
sentences.chinese: 在太空竞赛时期，美国和苏联曾争相创造航天领域的多个“第一”。

sentences.english: The Soviet Union released Sputnik 1, an artificial satellite, before anyone else, and the US landed on the Moon first.
sentences.chinese: 苏联率先发射了人类第一颗人造卫星“斯普特尼克1号”，而美国则率先实现了载人登月。

sentences.english: Now it appears that Mars is the celestial body of desire.
sentences.chinese: 如今，火星似乎成了众望所归的探索目标。

sentences.english: While the kudos and bragging rights to be the first nation to touchdown is an obvious draw, there are other reasons we want to get there.
sentences.chinese: 成为首个登陆火星的国家所带来的荣誉与吹嘘的资本，显然是一大吸引力，但我们探索火星还有其他原因。

sentences.english: One of these could be the survival of our species.
sentences.chinese: 其中之一可能关乎人类物种的延续。

sentences.english: You only have to look at the fossilised remains of the dinosaurs to see the benefit of finding another habitable planet.
sentences.chinese: 只需看看恐龙的化石残骸，就能明白找到另一颗宜居星球的重要意义。

sentences.english: While Mars doesn’t have the right conditions to call it home just yet, there’s always the concept of terraforming – changing the environment of a planet to suit our needs.
sentences.chinese: 虽然火星目前还不具备供人类定居的条件，但“地球化改造”的构想始终存在——也就是改造行星的环境，使其满足人类的生存需求。
但并非所有人都认同这一构想。

sentences.english: Leading astrophysicist Neil deGrasse Tyson has said the concept of altering habitability of another planet because of the damage we have done to Earth makes no sense when we can simply terraform Earth.
sentences.chinese: 顶尖天体物理学家尼尔·德格拉斯·泰森就曾表示，既然我们完全可以对地球进行生态改造，那么因人类对地球造成了破坏，就去改造另一颗行星使其宜居的想法，根本毫无道理。

sentences.english: It seems the main reason at the moment is the search for extraterrestrial life.
sentences.chinese: 目前来看，探索火星的主要原因似乎是为了寻找外星生命。

sentences.english: It has long been believed that, at one time, Mars was abundant with life.
sentences.chinese: 长期以来，人们一直认为火星曾生机勃勃。

sentences.english: Now seemingly dead, the potential fossils could answer questions about our own evolution and that of our planet.
sentences.chinese: 如今这颗星球看似一片死寂，但可能存在的化石，或许能解答关于人类及地球自身进化的诸多疑问。

sentences.english: One theory is that bacterial life on our planet didn’t start here, but was transferred via asteroid from Mars.
sentences.chinese: 有一种理论认为，地球上的细菌生命并非起源于地球，而是通过小行星从火星传播而来的。

sentences.english: One benefit championed by scientists like Neil deGrasse Tyson is that landing on Mars may inspire more people to become interested in science and astronomy.
sentences.chinese: 尼尔·德格拉斯·泰森等科学家推崇的一点是，登陆火星或许能激发更多人对科学和天文学的兴趣。

sentences.english: Surely inspiring a new generation to visit the stars is reason enough.
sentences.chinese: 显然，激励新一代人去探索星辰大海，这本身就已是足够充分的理由。
